what_it_does.name: mcp-builder
what_it_does.summary: A guide in four phases for creating MCP servers that let LLMs use external services through well-designed tools, with reference guides for TypeScript SDK v2, TypeScript SDK v1, Python FastMCP and MCP best practices. It covers research and planning, implementation of tools with input schemas, pagination and actionable errors, then build and test with npm run build, py_compile and the MCP Inspector. It ends with ten evaluation questions in an XML file and a Python harness that runs them against the server with Claude and writes a report. Use it when building MCP servers to integrate external APIs or services in Python or Node/TypeScript.
tasks: research the MCP specification, SDK docs and the target service's API
set up a TypeScript or Python MCP server project
implement tools with schemas, annotations, pagination and actionable errors
build and test the server with npm run build, py_compile and the MCP Inspector
migrate a TypeScript SDK v1 project to v2 with the codemod
write 10 read-only evaluation questions in an XML file
run the evaluation harness over stdio, sse or http and read the report
what_it_does.author_description: Guide for creating high-quality MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers that enable LLMs to interact with external services through well-designed tools. Use when building MCP servers to integrate external APIs or services, whether in Python (FastMCP) or Node/TypeScript (MCP SDK).

risks.risk: Instructions planted in fetched SDK READMEs or GitHub-hosted documentation reach the agent, since the workflow loads these externally authored files with WebFetch.
A crafted question in the evaluation XML file can steer the evaluation agent and the server tools it holds, since question text goes to the model without boundary markers or sanitisation.
risks.mitigation: none in the files, C2 notes that no boundary markers or sanitisation are applied

risks.risk: The harness runs whatever command and arguments are given with -c and -a as a local process with the user's privileges.
risks.mitigation: the command must be given explicitly on the command line, as C2 notes

risks.risk: A Streamable HTTP server exposed beyond localhost without bearer auth accepts tool calls from anyone who reaches it, since the handler verifies no tokens.
risks.mitigation: requireBearerAuth and Host and Origin validation, shown in the v2 guide, in place only when the builder adds them

risks.risk: Evaluation runs against a live service can change its data when the agent calls a state-changing tool, since the harness passes every tool of the server to the model.
risks.mitigation: questions must need only read-only operations, a rule for the question author, not enforced by the harness

risks.risk: Tokens and API keys given with -e or -H stay in shell history or logs, as the examples pass GITHUB_TOKEN and a bearer token on the command line.

limitations: TypeScript SDK v1 receives bug and security fixes only, and v1 code samples do not apply to v2.
SDK v2 does not support Zod 3, and Zod 4.0 to 4.1 schemas fail to type-check in registerTool.
A factory that returns one shared McpServer instance fails concurrent HTTP requests with -32603 Internal server error.
One console.log in a stdio server corrupts the JSON-RPC stream.
Tool annotations are hints, not security guarantees.
SSE is deprecated in favor of Streamable HTTP.
For sse and http transports the server must be started separately before the evaluation runs.
The harness scores answers by direct string comparison, so answers must be single verifiable values.

known_problems.workaround: verify the stdio command and arguments, or the URL and headers, and that required API keys are set
review the agent's feedback, tool descriptions, parameter docs, returned data size and error messages
use a more capable model, check returned data size and pagination, simplify the questions

known_problems.problem: the codemod could not rewrite some spots safely
known_problems.workaround: find them with grep -rn '@mcp-codemod-error' . and fix them, then run npx tsc --noEmit

known_problems.problem: the SDK drops .describe() text or logs a fallback warning with an older Zod
